title: Hajime_Botnet_Investigation_30a
description: Investigate and respond to Hajime botnet activity in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:

- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim machine for any unauthorized or suspicious services that might be responsible for periodic external communication. Identify the service name.
levels.solution: Check running services and system logs for any unusual network activity. The service name must be identified and reported. Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all services and look for any suspicious ones. The final flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and system logs for any unusual network activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all services and look for any suspicious ones.

levels.title: Identify C2 Port
levels.content: Determine the network port used for suspicious command-and-control communication on the victim machine. Identify the port number.
levels.solution: Analyze network connections and logs to identify unusual outbound connections. The C2 port number must be identified and reported. Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all network connections and look for any suspicious ports. The final flag is the port number.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze network connections and logs to identify unusual outbound connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for ports that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all network connections and look for any suspicious ports.

levels.title: Identify Target of Suspicious Traffic
levels.content: Identify the system receiving the abnormal volume of network traffic generated by the compromised host. Identify the IP address.
levels.solution: Examine network flows and logs to determine the target of the suspicious traffic. The victim IP address must be identified and reported. Use the command 'tcpdump -i any' to capture network traffic and look for any suspicious IP addresses. The final flag is the IP address.
